label: Teltonika RUTX08 (EOL)
description: A four-port gigabit VPN router with no cellular modem and no Wi-Fi: 1 WAN (reconfigurable as LAN) + 3 LAN, all gigabit. A wired router for a branch office that already has its uplink.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTX08 datasheet: 1 x WAN port (can be configured as LAN) 10/100/1000 Mbps and 3 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps, IEEE 802.3/802.3u. No cellular modem and no Wi-Fi: the datasheet contains no 802.11 wireless section, so neither is claimed. End of life per the vendor, kept in the catalogue because these are still in racks.

label: Teltonika RUTX09 (EOL)
description: A four-port gigabit LTE Cat 6 router: 1 WAN + 3 LAN at gigabit, no Wi-Fi. The wired cellular router - the modem is the uplink, so there is no radio to model.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTX09 datasheet: 1 x WAN port 10/100/1000 Mbps, 3 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps, described as four Gigabit Ethernet ports; LTE Cat 6, modelled at the 300 Mbps downlink class. No Wi-Fi: the datasheet's only 802.11 reference is 802.11e QoS on the Ethernet bridge, not a radio.

label: Teltonika RUTX10 (EOL)
description: The enterprise wired router: 1 WAN (reconfigurable as LAN) + 3 LAN at gigabit, dual-band 802.11ac Wave 2 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE, with no cellular modem.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTX10 datasheet: 1x WAN port (can be configured as LAN) 10/100/1000 Mbps and 3x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps; Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n/ac Wave 2 (Wi-Fi 5) dual band at up to 867 Mbps with MU-MIMO, plus Bluetooth LE. No cellular modem.

label: Teltonika RUTX12 (EOL)
description: Two LTE Cat 6 modems in one box with 1 WAN (reconfigurable as LAN) + 4 LAN at gigabit and dual-band 802.11ac. Built to bond or fail over between two carriers at once.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTX12 datasheet: 4 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps plus a WAN port (can be configured as LAN) at 10/100/1000 Mbps; Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n/ac (Wi-Fi 5) dual band up to 867 Mbps; two LTE Cat 6 modems, so two cellular interfaces are modelled at the 300 Mbps class each.

label: Teltonika RUTX14 (EOL)
description: An LTE Cat 12 router with 1 WAN (reconfigurable as LAN) + 4 LAN at gigabit and dual-band 802.11ac. The Cat 12 modem is the reason for the 600M cellular interface against the Cat 6 units' 300M.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTX14 datasheet: 1 x WAN port (can be configured as LAN) 10/100/1000 Mbps and 4 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps; 802.11ac dual band Wi-Fi; LTE Cat 12, modelled at the 600 Mbps downlink class - three times the Cat 4 units in this catalogue and twice the Cat 6 ones.

label: Teltonika TRB140
description: A tiny industrial 4G gateway: one Gigabit Ethernet port, a micro-USB and RutOS. It is a modem with an Ethernet face - there is no switch and no radio.
notes: Vendor figures (Teltonika wiki and TRB140 datasheet): one Gigabit Ethernet port plus Micro-USB; 4G LTE Cat 4. No Wi-Fi and no switch fabric, so a single eth0 is the whole data path.

label: Teltonika TRB245
description: An industrial M2M 4G gateway with one 10/100 Ethernet port that can be used as WAN or LAN, plus digital inputs, a relay and a serial interface. One port, so the routing decision is which side it is on.
notes: Vendor figures from the TRB245 datasheet: 1 x LAN port 10/100 Mbps, IEEE 802.3/802.3u, which the vendor notes can be used as a WAN port; 4G LTE Cat 4; digital inputs, relay output and RS232/RS485. Named lan1 rather than wan because the vendor's default role is LAN.

label: Teltonika TRB255
description: An industrial M2M gateway with one 10/100 Ethernet port and RS232/RS485: a 4G modem that speaks to legacy serial equipment.
notes: Vendor figures from the TRB255 datasheet: 1 x LAN port 10/100 Mbps, IEEE 802.3/802.3u; RS232 and RS485; 4G LTE Cat 4. Serial ports modelled as console interfaces, as elsewhere in the Teltonika range.
